notes: Heat pump point dictionary. Air-side and compressor points carry from the AHU/RTU dictionaries; HP-specific points grep-verified against Brick 1.4.4 where a class exists (Thermal_Power_Sensor, Active_Power_Sensor, Mode_Command) and provisional where none does (defrost_status). Owning equipment: the packaged heat pump unit. EXPANSION 2026-08-17: refrigerant-side points added for the future charge-fault family (NIST SP 1087 grounding); the two saturation temperatures are HOST-DERIVED virtual points per SCHEMA.md's virtual-point convention.

points.name: thermal_power
points.description: Delivered thermal output (heating or cooling), kW

s223.pattern: Sensor observes QuantifiableObservableProperty on the unit via hasProperty

points.notes: brick:Thermal_Power_Sensor grep-verified in Brick 1.4.4. Usually a host-computed virtual point (airflow x cp x deltaT or refrigerant-side); HP-FC-050 consumes it as the COP numerator, and the fit quality of the host's baseline depends on it — treat its provenance as part of the baseline R^2 precondition.

points.name: elec_power

s223.pattern: Sensor observes QuantifiableObservableProperty on the compressor circuit via hasProperty

points.notes: Brick 1.4.4 has no Electrical_Power_Sensor class; Active_Power_Sensor (verified) is the correct real-power reading. Bind the compressor circuit, not the whole unit, or fan energy pollutes the COP.

points.name: oat

s223.pattern: Sensor observes QuantifiableObservableProperty at the outdoor-air intake

points.notes: Brick spelling is Outside_ (Outdoor_Air_Temperature_Sensor does not exist). Role-OutdoorAirIntake is 223P's only outdoor role; used by reference instance oa-temp. [HP dictionary] Brick class and 223P pattern carried over (equipment-independent); used by the COP baseline (regression axis) and defrost sanity test.

points.name: sat

s223.pattern: Sensor observes QuantifiableObservableProperty attached to the AHU supply-air OutletConnectionPoint

points.notes: Brick Discharge_Air_Temperature_Sensor is brick:aliasOf this class. 223P pattern verbatim from reference instance MultipleZoneAhu-sa-temp; medium comes from hasMedium on the owning ConnectionPoint. [HP dictionary] Brick class and 223P pattern carried over (equipment-independent); for HP-FC-052 the discharge temperature is the reversing-valve witness.

points.name: comp_status
points.description: Compressor run status (true = at least one compressor running)

s223.pattern: EnumeratedObservableProperty on the Compressor via hasProperty

points.notes: Brick 1.4.4 has no Compressor_Run_Status class; the honest mapping is the generic On_Off_Status attached via isPointOf to brick:Compressor (class verified). On multi-compressor units, rules that ask whether ANY compressor is running (RTU-FC-052) may bind the OR of the individual statuses; RTU-FC-050 counts rising edges, and an OR UNDERCOUNTS cycling — a lag-compressor start while the lead is already running never moves the OR, so a two-stage unit can short-cycle its lag circuit and read healthy. Bind RTU-FC-050 per compressor. 223P pattern mirrors sf_status's Binary-OnOff enumeration; no packaged-unit reference instance checked. [HP dictionary] Brick class and 223P pattern carried over (equipment-independent); same per-compressor binding caveat as RTU-FC-050.

points.name: defrost_status
points.description: Defrost cycle active (true while the unit is in defrost)

s223.pattern: EnumeratedObservableProperty (Binary-OnOff) on the defrost sequence via hasProperty

points.notes: Brick 1.4.4 has no Defrost_Status class (grep-verified absent); bind the BAS/unit defrost-active flag and tag the generic Status pattern. Sampling caveat for HP-FC-051: a defrost cycle shorter than the host tick is invisible to the edge counter — tick well below the ~5-10 min cycle length.

points.name: mode_command
points.description: Commanded operating mode (host-mapped integer; library encoding 1 = HEATING, 2 = COOLING)

s223.pattern: EnumeratedActuatableProperty on the unit via hasProperty

points.notes: brick:Mode_Command grep-verified in Brick 1.4.4. The 1/2 encoding is this library's convention (expected_mode precedent); HP-FC-052 exposes both codes as rule params so hosts with their own enum rebind without editing the graph.

points.name: suction_temp
points.description: Compressor suction line refrigerant temperature (surface-mount acceptable)

s223.pattern: QuantifiableObservableProperty on the equipment via hasProperty

points.notes: No Brick 1.4.4 suction-temperature class (only Refrigerant_Level_Sensor exists refrigerant-side); null mapping per defrost_status precedent. Superheat = suction_temp - evap_sat_temp.

points.name: liquid_temp

s223.pattern: QuantifiableObservableProperty on the equipment via hasProperty

points.notes: No Brick 1.4.4 class; null mapping. Subcooling = cond_sat_temp - liquid_temp.

points.name: evap_sat_temp
points.description: Evaporating saturation temperature (HOST-DERIVED: suction pressure via refrigerant P-T lookup, or coil-surface proxy)

s223.pattern: QuantifiableObservableProperty on the equipment via hasProperty

points.notes: HOST-DERIVED virtual point (zone_reheat_fraction/chw_valve_max precedent): the P-T relationship is refrigerant-specific and lives at the host, never in a rule graph. Derivation MUST match the site's refrigerant.

points.name: cond_sat_temp
points.description: Condensing saturation temperature (HOST-DERIVED: discharge/liquid pressure via refrigerant P-T lookup)

s223.pattern: QuantifiableObservableProperty on the equipment via hasProperty

points.notes: HOST-DERIVED virtual point, same convention and refrigerant caveat as evap_sat_temp.

points.name: comp_discharge_temp
points.description: Compressor discharge line refrigerant temperature (surface-mount acceptable)

s223.pattern: QuantifiableObservableProperty on the equipment via hasProperty

points.notes: No Brick 1.4.4 class models refrigerant-line temperatures (suction_temp precedent; discharge-AIR classes are the wrong medium). Refrigerant side, hot-gas line between compressor and reversing valve. Consumed by the reversing-valve internal-leakage rule (HP-FC-055): NIST SP 1087 (2012) found leakage raises discharge and evaporating temperature while condensing temperature and subcooling fall, with superheat unaffected.
